purpose: Establish one deterministic RISC-V toolchain discovery and configuration mechanism for every project driver, with explicit precedence, validation of the selected compiler, fail-closed overrides, and negative controls
rtl_note: No RTL, testbench or acceptance criterion was changed by this run. The RTL/testbench entries in dirty_files predate RUN-0010 (F1/F3) and are carried unchanged.

resolved_toolchain.version: riscv-none-elf-gcc.exe (xPack GNU RISC-V Embedded GCC x86_64) 12.2.0

unified_scripts.role: firmware build; resolves via findToolchain(), prints gcc path/source/version
firmware build; delegates resolution to toolchain.js --json, no local discovery
ROM/TCM hex generation; resolves via findToolchain() (pre-existing)
E2E; hardcoded xpack path removed, resolves once and exports RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_BIN to children
unified gate; tools stage now resolves and records the RISC-V toolchain and blocks if it fails
regression; builds images via build_fw.js and records the resolved compiler in its log

precedence: known prefixes on PATH (absolute path reported)
outcome: F6 PASS — one resolver, validated selection, fail-closed overrides, every affected flow verified on the same xPack GCC 12.2.0-2
interpretation: The four entry points that used to disagree now either call the shared resolver or delegate to a driver that does. Explicit configuration is validated and never silently replaced: a bad RISCV_GCC_PREFIX, bad RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_BIN, or a prefix/bin pair that disagrees exits 2 with a message naming the variable. The gate's tools stage proves the toolchain before any stage runs, and the regression and build logs now name the exact compiler that produced the images being tested.
limitations: Verified on Windows only (win32, Git Bash); the POSIX branch of installedDirs() is implemented but was not executed.

No second RISC-V toolchain and no host gcc exist on this machine, so the conflict control uses a prefix the installed bin directory does not contain; two valid but different toolchains were not available to compare.

A real wrong-target compiler binary could not be produced (no host compiler to rename), so rejection of non-RISC-V target strings is unit-tested through isRiscvMachine() and the broken-executable control, not against a mislabelled genuine compiler.
build_fw.py now writes to build/fw/ instead of scripts/fw_build/build/ so both drivers produce the same artefact; the old private output directory is not migrated or cleaned.
build_fw.py requires node on PATH because it delegates resolution; if node is absent it exits 2 rather than guessing a prefix.
build_fw.bat requires cmd.exe; on POSIX the Node/Python drivers are the entry points.
Self-reviewed only; no independent evaluator exists in this environment.
